paper_metadata.title: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Networks for Real-Time Financial Fraud Detection: A Novel Framework with Temporal Correlation Analysis

summary: The paper reports AQEN on a 5,000-transaction synthetic fraud dataset with 8 features, achieving 0.947 accuracy, 0.812 precision, 0.798 recall, 0.805 F1, and 0.951 AUC, versus XGBoost at 0.935 accuracy and 0.923 AUC. The quantum circuit uses 8 qubits, 47 physical layers, 7 CNOTs, 1024 shots, and is evaluated only on Qiskit AerSimulator with an IBMQ Lima noise model; the strongest classical baseline remains competitive and the result is simulation-only.

experiments.description: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Networks (AQEN) for real-time financial fraud detection on synthetic and benchmark transaction datasets, evaluated against classical baselines and quantum ablations (QFCC, standard VQC) using Qiskit Aer simulation with an IBMQ Lima noise model.

algorithm.variant: Adaptive Quantum Entanglement Networks (AQEN) / Quantum Fraud Correlation Circuit (QFCC)
algorithm.parameter_initialization: fixed seeds for all circuit initializations; quantum-aware initialization

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 8 primary transaction features mapped to rotation angles; temporal features encoded via sliding-window history; qubits 0-3 encode amount/velocity/risk/network features, qubits 4-6 temporal correlation processing, qubit 7 auxiliary/measurement
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize fraud classification loss / maximize fraud probability separation between fraudulent and legitimate transactions
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: adaptive entanglement regularization; no explicit hard constraints reported

problem_instance.description: Financial fraud detection on transaction streams with temporal and network correlations
problem_instance.dataset_name: Synthetic financial dataset; IEEE-CIS; Credit Card (Kaggle); Synthetic Temporal

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic dataset with 8% fraud rate and 8 primary features; IEEE-CIS reduced to 12 dimensions via PCA; Credit Card dataset with 30 anonymized features; Synthetic Temporal with 8 engineered temporal features

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: continuous features normalized to [0, π]; temporal correlation features via sliding-window analysis; network-based features from graph analysis; IEEE-CIS PCA to 12 dimensions
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 20 independent runs for paired t-tests; 50 runs for Wilcoxon signed-rank test in appendix; bootstrap with 10,000 resamples for 95% CI; fixed seeds 42, 123, 456, 789, 2025 in appendix

implementation_details.transpilation_target: IBM Q Lima native set {RZ, SX, CNOT}
implementation_details.classical_solver: scikit-learn baselines and XGBoost for comparison
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: feature engineering, temporal aggregations, polynomial interactions, domain-specific fraud indicators; stratified cross-validation for baselines
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: thresholding/classification metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC)

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: smooth decrease with close training/validation tracking

results.uncertainty: 95% CI [0.8%, 1.6%] for the improvement over XGBoost; p < 0.001

speedup_claims.conditions: training time on the reported synthetic financial dataset under the stated Qiskit AerSimulator + IBMQ Lima noise model setup
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as wall-clock training time averaged over 20 runs; quantum compilation time (~0.15 s per circuit) excluded from inference timing.

speedup_claims.conditions: per-transaction inference latency on the reported synthetic financial dataset
speedup_claims.caveats: Inference latency measured by batch processing 10,000 transactions and dividing by 10,000; quantum simulation was single-threaded while classical baselines used 48 CPU cores.
Memory usage values reported as 45 MB vs 320 MB.
Derived from ROC AUC difference; not a direct runtime speedup.
Presented as a corollary/theoretical estimate, not experimentally validated.

speedup_claims.conditions: for realistic parameters d = 100, τ = 10, q = 8
speedup_claims.caveats: Stated as a corollary; not directly measured in experiments.

speedup_claims.factor: O(n · q^2 · τ · log d) training vs O(n · d^2 · τ^3) classical
speedup_claims.conditions: asymptotic complexity analysis under the paper's assumptions
speedup_claims.caveats: Asymptotic claim; depends on structured temporal correlations and q = O(log d).

speedup_claims.factor: O(q^2 · τ · log d) inference vs O(d^2 · τ^3) classical
speedup_claims.conditions: asymptotic complexity analysis under the paper's assumptions
speedup_claims.caveats: Asymptotic claim; not a measured runtime speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: O(q^2 + τ · d) memory vs O(d^2 · τ^2) classical
speedup_claims.conditions: asymptotic complexity analysis under the paper's assumptions
speedup_claims.caveats: Asymptotic claim; not a measured memory benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n · q2 · τ · log d) training; O(q2 · τ · log d) inference; O(q2 + τ · d) memory
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(n · d2 · τ3) training; O(d2 · τ3) inference; O(d2 · τ2) memory
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: 1.8 s training; 0.12 ms inference per transaction
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: 12.1 s training (XGBoost); 0.89 ms inference per transaction (XGBoost)

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: 8 logical qubits, 47 physical layers, 7 CNOTs, 1024 shots, noisy simulation with IBMQ Lima noise model
limiting_factors: No real quantum hardware execution; only AerSimulator with noise model
Classical baselines remain strong and are not clearly beaten on all reported metrics by a practically deployable quantum system
Reported gains are on a small synthetic/benchmark fraud-detection setup
Circuit depth and noise sensitivity limit NISQ practicality
No crossover analysis or asymptotic advantage over best classical method is established

notes: Hardware type inferred from explicit use of Qiskit AerSimulator with IBMQ Lima noise model; no real QPU execution is reported.
Gate count total inferred from appendix counts: 156 single-qubit (RZ/SX equivalents) + 7 CNOT = 163 total gates.
Circuit depth reported as 47 physical layers in appendix and main text.

Speedup order is polynomial_other because the paper reports constant-factor/runtime improvements and asymptotic polynomial scaling claims, not a proven asymptotic quantum speedup over the best classical method.
num_variational_params not explicitly reported; AQEN/QFCC uses multiple trainable angles but the exact count is not stated.

The paper claims quantum advantage and reports AQEN outperforming XGBoost on accuracy, precision, recall, F1, AUC, and runtime in simulation, but the evidence is limited to noisy simulation and a small benchmark setting.
This does not establish practical advantage on meaningful problem size under Hoefler-style constant-factor scrutiny.
